lesson.title: Collision Lab: Momentum Conservation
lesson.buzzAssessmentTitle: Unit 3 Lesson 4: Collision Lab - Momentum Conservation

gradingDesign.rule: Only lessons with a completed provided chart use 10 automatic points; variable student evidence is graded in the final two BusyBee responses.

questions.prompt: Trial 1 total momentum before the collision: ________ kg*m/s
Trial 1 total momentum after the collision: ________ kg*m/s
Trial 2 total momentum before the collision: ________ kg*m/s
Trial 2 total momentum after the collision: ________ kg*m/s
Trial 3 total momentum before the collision: ________ kg*m/s
Trial 3 total momentum after the collision: ________ kg*m/s
Trial 4 total momentum before the collision: ________ kg*m/s
Trial 4 total momentum after the collision: ________ kg*m/s
Trial 5 total momentum before the collision: ________ kg*m/s
Trial 5 total momentum after the collision: ________ kg*m/s
Use at least two trials from your completed charts to explain what happened to total momentum as elasticity changed from 100% to 50% to 0%.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: The response must use trial totals and distinguish momentum conservation from elasticity.
a. Full credit: Cites accurate before-and-after totals from at least two trials and explains that total momentum stayed constant for elastic, partially inelastic, and perfectly inelastic collisions.
  Partial credit: States the correct conservation pattern but gives only one trial or incomplete numerical evidence.
  No credit: Claims that momentum is lost when elasticity decreases or gives no chart evidence.

questions.prompt: Trial 2 has moving balls but zero total momentum. Explain how that is possible, why total velocity is not the conserved quantity, and why everyday objects may later come to rest even though momentum was conserved during the collision.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Look for vector cancellation, the role of mass, and outside forces after the collision.
a. Full credit: Uses the equal and opposite Trial 2 momenta to explain a zero system total, states that momentum m*v rather than the sum of velocities is conserved, and explains that friction transfers momentum to the surroundings after the collision.
  Partial credit: Correctly explains two of the three required ideas.
  No credit: Treats momentum as a scalar or says the collision itself destroys momentum.
